title: Technology Sector Update for 08/13/2018: VSAT,HQCL,JKS,TIVO,ATUS
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -0.50%
AAPL +0.90%
IBM -1.02%
CSCO +0.15%
GOOG +0.15%
Technology stocks have turned higher in late Monday trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding just over 0.1% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising more than 0.3%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ ViaSat ( VSAT ) was about 5% higher in late Monday trading, easing somewhat from a more than 6% advance previously in the session despite analysts at Needham & Co today trimming their price target for broadband network equipment company by $4 to $70 while keeping their Buy rating for the company's stock. The company last week reported its fiscal Q1 financial results, with Needham expecting ViaSat to produce better margins and "sharply ramping" earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization as well as subpar subscriber data for the just completed quarter and a disappointing forecast for the current quarter.
In other sector news:
+ Hanwha Q CELLS Co Ltd ( HQCL ) has given up its slim gain in recent trading and was retracing a portion of a nearly 1% decline earlier in the session that followed the South Korean manufacturer of solar-power modules reporting Q2 revenue exceeding Wall Street expectations and projecting Q3 revenue topping analyst estimates. Revenue totaled $518.4 million during the three months ended June 30, down from $577.7 million during the same quarter last year but still beating the Capital IQ consensus by around $18.1 million. The company sees Q3 revenue in range of $590 million to $610 million, surpassing the analyst mean by at least $20.1 million. It also recorded a Q2 net loss of $0.50 per American depositary share compared with a $0.22 per ADS profit during the year-ago period and missing the Street view looking for a $0.11 per share in net income.
- TiVo ( TIVO ) was lower Monday afternoon, dropping almost 3% in recent trading, after saying Altice's ( USAT ) European corporate cousin in Portugal has renewed its multi-yearintellectual property license with the video-recording company, helping build momentum for its intellectual property portfolio throughout the region.
- JinkoSolar Holding Company ( JKS ) slumped Monday, at one point sinking over 20%, after the photovoltaic products company reported a hefty drop in Q2 revenue compared with year-ago levels. The company generated RMB6.06 billion, or about $915.9 million, in total revenue during the April-to-June fiscal period, down from RMB7.92 billion in the year-ago quarter but still topping the Capital IQ consensus expecting $909.1 million in quarterly revenue. Excluding one-time items, JinkoSolar also posted non-GAAP net income of RMB2.73, or about $0.41, per American depositary share, improving on an RMB1.91 per ADS adjusted profit during the same quarter last year and beating the $0.33 per ADS analyst mean.
